scope: Fresh reverse-engineering and software binary-analysis tools, with emphasis on source reconstruction, static recompilation, and underrepresented embedded instruction sets. The game-specific entry is an application tool; it does not add a game title.

projects.title: decomp.wtf
projects.game: Game binaries and community decompilation projects (multi-title tool)
projects.platform: Linux; Windows via WSL 2 (documented as unstable); macOS unsupported. From-scratch inputs include GameCube/Wii and Nintendo 64 (recommended), plus beta PlayStation 1/2, Game Boy Advance, and Nintendo DS ROMs/discs/program files.
projects.status: Discontinued and archived. The maintainer says no further issue fixes, pull-request reviews, or releases are planned; v0.10.6 is identified as the last installable version. The README labels GameCube/Wii and N64 as the recommended paths; PS1/PS2/GBA/DS remain beta.
projects.summary: Local GUI and MCP application that coordinates agents to reconstruct C/C++ functions from user-supplied game binaries or existing community decomp projects. Each candidate is built with the target project’s original compiler and checked byte-for-byte against the original function or project build; matched output can be exported as a rebuildable source tree. It does not provide ROMs or game code.
projects.strategy: Per-function matching source reconstruction: splat/spimdisasm or platform-specific analyzers locate code; an agent drafts C/C++; pinned original compilers build it; the result is linked at the original address and checked byte-for-byte. Public project forks use their own build and objdiff checks. This is a matching decompiler workflow, not a machine-code static recompiler.
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed Python application source. Requires the user’s own game ROM/disc/program file or a checkout of a supported public decomp project; no copyrighted game binary or assets are included. Some proprietary compiler toolchains are optional and installed only after user acceptance.
projects.subtype: Local matching-decompilation GUI and MCP workflow for game software

projects.title: WinRecomp
projects.game: PE32/i386 Windows application binaries (multi-title recompilation tool)
projects.platform: 32-bit i386 Windows PE executables → generated native Windows x64 CMake projects. Linux builds support analysis/diagnostics; the documented E3 Windows API integration is targeted at Windows x64.
projects.status: Early development; the README describes runtime version 0.2 and seven verified roadmap gates totaling 50/100 planning points. Synthetic translated programs, including a GUI/framebuffer comparison, are tested on Windows. An E3-derived x64 executable has been generated, but the maintainer explicitly says actual E3 Windows startup, rendering, and gameplay are unverified; there is no universal PE32 compatibility claim.
projects.summary: Static recompilation tool for bounded PE32/i386 Windows executables. It analyzes guest code and emits C++ instruction translations plus a CMake project that preserves 32-bit guest state while building for native Windows x64. Unsupported instructions, imports, and indirect transfers stop with errors rather than silently becoming no-ops. The repository contains synthetic fixtures, not a proprietary target executable or its assets.
projects.strategy: PE32/i386 analysis and bounded static lifting to C++, linked with a runtime that models guest memory, registers, imports, and selected Win32 APIs; generated code is built for Windows x64 and exercised against guest/native conformance fixtures.
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed C++ source. The analyst supplies the original PE32 executable and any application data/assets; game-derived binaries and generated source stay local according to the README.

projects.title: Fission
projects.game: Native machine-code binaries (multi-format analysis and source-recovery tool)
projects.platform: The current strongest documented evaluation path is Windows x86-64 PE. The loader and committed Sleigh specifications provide other binary-format and instruction coverage, but the README cautions against broad architecture-parity claims.
projects.status: Active; latest tagged release found is v0.2.3 (2026-08-28), with source commits through 2026-10-15. The README says its long-term rebuildable-source target is not reached: one tested binary’s 68 decompiled functions currently produce 20 missing/duplicate declaration errors when compiled together.
projects.summary: Rust-native binary-analysis workspace that loads executable images, lifts instruction semantics through committed Ghidra-style Sleigh specifications to p-code, then applies its own intermediate representations, control-flow structuring, type recovery, and source rendering. Its execution differential checks reconstructed behavior; current source output is an early prototype and has not yet rebuilt the tested binary as a unit.
projects.strategy: Sleigh-based instruction decoding and semantic lifting through p-code into NIR/HIR, followed by CFG structuring, type recovery, and source emission; validates function behavior by executing the emitted body and comparing it with machine code.
projects.source_available: Public Apache-2.0 Rust source. Analysts supply binaries for examination; the project keeps its Sleigh specifications and signature data in the repository and does not include proprietary target applications.
projects.subtype: Semantics-first binary analysis and experimental rebuildable source reconstruction

projects.title: C166/ST10 Architecture Plugin for Binary Ninja
projects.game: Infineon C166 / STMicro ST10 embedded firmware
projects.platform: Infineon C166-classic, C166-vx, C166-v2, and ST10 firmware; Binary Ninja plugin binaries are published for Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS x64, and macOS ARM64.
projects.status: Maintained; release stable-6.0.10601 was published 2026-09-09. The README reports full instruction disassembly and only partial lifting to Binary Ninja Low Level IL, so some instruction semantics and resulting decompilation remain unsupported.
projects.summary: Binary Ninja architecture plugin for analyzing embedded firmware built for the Infineon C166 and STMicro ST10 instruction families. It adds disassembly, partial Low Level IL semantics, calling conventions, and extended-mode/data-page register support. Analysis requires a compatible Binary Ninja installation and a user-provided firmware image.
projects.strategy: Architecture plugin that decodes C166/ST10 instructions and supplies partial Binary Ninja LLIL semantics, with C166 calling-convention and extended DPP/EXT state support; it enables binary analysis but does not provide a complete source reconstruction.
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed C++ source and release binaries. Requires Binary Ninja 5.1.8104 or later and user-supplied firmware; the Binary Ninja analysis application is a separate dependency.
projects.subtype: Embedded C166/ST10 disassembler and partial lifter plugin
